as_told.title: How the UAP Task Force was set up to hunt down legacy programs

plain: The analyst Matthew Pines tells Michels that the government's UFO inquiry "started really rolling" in 2019 and 2020. That was when the UAP Task Force, a Pentagon group set up to study unidentified anomalous phenomena (the official term for UFOs), began work under orders from Congress written into the National Defense Authorization Act, the yearly law that funds the military. In Pines's account, Congress set up the group after news stories in 2017 and 2018 and some quiet back-channel conversations, and gave it the job of tracking down old secret programs, while a former intelligence officer named David Grusch and a colleague named Karl Nell pieced the story together from inside.
